level_gate::steep_ge_median.fable_too_good_finding: The probe's own wf_stable check only tests SIGN of expectancy per half, not concentration. Splitting the walk-forward halves shows BOTH are independently CONCENTRATED: first_half n=11, exp=$158.45/tr, top3day%=171.8%; second_half n=234, exp=$11.70/tr, top3day%=180.8%. The pooled top3day%=121.4% (<150% threshold) is an artifact of averaging two fragile halves, not a robust edge.

rows.bh_fdr: 0/8 gate variants (all 3 families combined) reject the null at q=0.10 -- FRED's best p=0.1072 (steep_ge_median / flat_lt_median, same two-sample test) does not survive m=8 correction
rows.verdict_reason: steep_ge_median superficially clears the probe script's own pooled heuristic (CLEAN + wf_stable=True) -- flagged and investigated per /fable-too-good because it was the ONE candidate of 8 that looked like it cleared. Root cause: the wf_stable check tests only the SIGN of each half's expectancy, not concentration, so two independently-fragile/CONCENTRATED halves (top3day% 171.8% and 180.8%, first half n=11) can pool into a nominally-CLEAN combined number. A Welch t-test on kept-vs-dropped PnL (p=0.107) does not distinguish the gated population from the ungated one, and fails BH-FDR at q=0.10 across the 8 variants tested this session. Real verdict is KILL, not the script's naive CLEAR.
